q1_issues.issue: The pre-nominal participial modifiers of 'the cocaine importing and money laundering gang' are expanded into asserted top-level import/launder events, but the instruction set treats a participle used as a modifier as an adjective and licenses the event (reduced-relative) form only for post-nominal participles.

'money laundering' is a fixed multi-word idiom whose literal reading is incoherent for these participants, so unpacking it into a literal launder event with 'money' as Patient is exactly the literal unpacking the idiom rule forbids.
The reduced relative 'investigating the ... gang' carries no status atom, so a specific past investigation is recorded as the generic/habitual default.

q2_gaps: compound pre-nominal participial modifier with an incorporated object ('the cocaine importing ... gang') — the instruction set covers post-nominal reduced relatives and participial modifiers as plain adjectives, but not an object-incorporating participial premodifier
tense of an untensed reduced relative inside a past-tense matrix — the instruction set gives no rule for whether the reduced-relative event inherits the matrix tense
notes: Count, group, compound genus (police_officer), the adjective-PP-complement state for 'involved in', the per-member distribution rule and the duration measure for 'two-year' are all handled per the instruction set. Predicating 'culmination' of the bust group symbol is defensible as a property of the collection itself.
